W6 model after E049. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. Noise: 3-seed accuracy ±0.2–0.3 pp on identical code (same-commit E036 reruns: 0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497, 0.7544). Time noise ±0.04 s, with build drift up to ~0.05 s.

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch or sample cuts (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048) trade at dial-like rates.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049), because frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. Late freezes are roughly neutral. Early ones are not (E037's cliff). E049 shows that cascade plus a top-up is net ~-0.13 s at neutral accuracy. This is the one lever that has kept working.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe is near a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by -0.1 pp.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047), so a ceiling for I076 is ~1%, and some of the copies are probably the cudagraph copy-in.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Activation swaps: GELU→ReLU is mostly bytes-bound, so it should save 1–3% and may cost accuracy.
8. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. This is the main decision noise.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E037, E041, E046, E048). Accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges, treat differences below 0.3 pp on 3 seeds as noise, and expect step-count cuts and freezes to save slightly more than linear scaling suggests.

Unsure: the true tip mean (0.752 ± 0.1), selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, how far the group-2 freeze can extend, and whether the stem's 31×31 work can be removed (I080).

forecasts.reason: The ceiling is ~1–2%, and rebuild noise on time and accuracy is comparable to the gain.
ReLU saves a little time since the kernels are bytes-bound, and probably costs some accuracy.
Dropping cudagraphs costs time. Bit-identical rebuilds are plausible only with a pinned cache, which may be disallowed.
A stride-2 conv drops the pool's max-over-4 and also the conv at 31×31. It saves real time but likely costs accuracy through a different function.
Selection plus a top-up is about on the dial line and within noise.
A longer group-2 freeze saves ~0.08 s, with a possible small accuracy loss that 3 seeds cannot resolve.

cruxes: Is the tip's true unselected mean ≥0.7515 on many seeds? That decides whether any further time cut is feasible at all.
Does the group-2 freeze dose extend past 10% (I082) at neutral accuracy? It is the only lever that has kept giving time.
Can build-to-build kernel reselection noise (~0.3 pp) be pinned? Without that, sub-0.15 pp keep decisions are unreliable.
